title: Gen Digital Built Norton Revamp News Engine on AWS Bedrock
summary: Gen Digital leverages Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search to power Norton Revamp's AI-curated news engine, delivering personalized content at scale.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Gen Digital deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search to build Norton Revamp's AI-curated news engine for personalized content delivery.
- The system processes real-time web data to match cybersecurity news with user preferences, improving engagement and relevance metrics.
- This implementation demonstrates how enterprise security brands leverage AWS's agentic AI infrastructure for consumer-facing media applications.


Gen Digital, the cybersecurity company behind Norton and Avast, has deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search to power the AI-curated news engine for Norton Revamp, its next-generation consumer security platform. Officially launched on November 3, 2026, the system delivers personalized cybersecurity news and threat intelligence to millions of Norton users through real-time web indexing and natural language processing.


## Architecture and Implementation


The Norton Revamp news engine leverages Amazon Bedrock's AgentCore framework to orchestrate web search, content retrieval, and relevance ranking. According to Gen Digital's engineering team, the system processes over 50,000 cybersecurity-related articles daily from verified sources, applying user preference models to surface the most relevant stories. The AgentCore Web Search API handles query expansion, semantic matching, and freshness scoring without requiring Gen Digital to maintain separate search infrastructure.


The implementation uses multiple foundation models available through Bedrock, including Claude for content summarization and a specialized embedding model for semantic similarity. Gen Digital reports a 40 percent improvement in click-through rates compared to its previous rule-based news feed, with average session time increasing by 22 percent since deployment.


## Personalization and Safety Controls


Norton Revamp's news engine applies three layers of personalization: threat relevance based on the user's device profile, content preferences learned from engagement history, and geographic context for localized threat intelligence. The system automatically filters misinformation and unverified sources using Bedrock's built-in guardrails, which Gen Digital customized to enforce cybersecurity industry standards.


- Real-time threat alerts prioritized by device vulnerability scanning
- Automated fact-checking against trusted security databases
- Configurable content filters for enterprise and family accounts


## Performance and Scalability


Gen Digital scaled the news engine to serve 180 million Norton users globally without building dedicated search clusters. The company pays only for active queries through Bedrock's consumption-based pricing, reducing infrastructure costs by an estimated 35 percent compared to self-hosted alternatives. Peak load during major security incidents reaches 12,000 queries per second, handled automatically by AWS's managed scaling.


The engineering team highlighted AgentCore's ability to chain multiple web searches within a single user query, enabling complex research tasks like "compare ransomware trends across Europe and Asia this quarter." This multi-step reasoning capability differentiates the Norton implementation from traditional keyword-based news feeds.


## What This Means


Gen Digital's deployment demonstrates how consumer security platforms are shifting from static threat databases to dynamic, AI-curated intelligence feeds. By building on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search rather than developing proprietary search infrastructure, the company accelerated time-to-market while maintaining enterprise-grade safety controls. This architecture pattern may influence how other cybersecurity vendors integrate generative AI into consumer products, particularly for applications requiring real-time web data and personalized content delivery at massive scale.
